open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct, from every source-consistent recorded stratum of the quadratic core, a bounded-circuit reduced local presentation of the source prime: equations of the correct codimension together with a Jacobian minor nonzero at the source generic point. Use that presentation to carry out the localized generic slice and to emit every required nonzero specialization and real-lifting certificate within the claimed fixed-parameter bound \(n^{C(k+1)}\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen quadratic-core lemma preserves the queried projection only extensionally. It does not assert generic reducedness, conormal generation, a bounded prime-component presentation, or a lifting identity. Source-parametric identity testing can choose zero versus nonzero divisor status and can reject extraneous factors after a finite annihilator is constructed, but it cannot manufacture a nonvanishing Jacobian minor when the available equations vanish nonreducedly along the source component. General radical or primary decomposition does not, from the stated premises, have the required \(n^{C(k+1)}\) arithmetic-circuit bound.
open_obligations.attempted: Extended the prior Jacobian-rank algebraicity test by localizing a source-consistent core stratum at the product of its nonzero recorded factors and a putative source-nonvanishing Jacobian minor. On that open set, a complementary generic affine slice is zero-dimensional and meets every queried-coordinate conjugate. The multiplication polynomial of the sliced union may contain extraneous factors, but factoring it and testing \(q(\lambda_e)=0\) by source substitution selects the unique minimal polynomial, so explicit prime-component selection is unnecessary after the localized reduced presentation exists. This route fails exactly because the frozen core gives no way to construct the reduced presentation or its nonvanishing minor at the promised complexity.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The already established algebraicity test and transcendental certificate can be strengthened by removing extraneous zero-dimensional factors without first isolating the source component.  Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\), with \(r\leq 2k\), denote the exposed coordinates of \(\mathsf{Core}_{G,e}\), and let
\[
 \xi:K_G[x]\longrightarrow L
\]
be evaluation at the corresponding source coefficients.  For one source-consistent recorded stratum, let \(J\subseteq K_G[x]\) be generated by the cleared core equations and by every recorded factor whose image under \(\xi\) is zero.  Let \(H\) be the product of the recorded factors whose images under \(\xi\) are nonzero.  Source-parametric polynomial identity testing distinguishes the two cases.  Since the localized generic-fiber algebra is integral, \(J\subseteq P:=\ker\xi\), and localization at \(H\) retains every conjugate of \(\lambda_e\) over \(K_G\).

Suppose that one has computed \(h_1,\ldots,h_c\in J\), where \(c=\operatorname{ht}P\), and a \(c\)-by-\(c\) minor \(\Delta\) of their Jacobian in \(x\) such that \(\xi(\Delta)\neq0\).  This displayed condition is not being assumed for the theorem; it identifies the remaining certificate that must be constructed.  On the principal open set \(D(H\Delta)\), the equations \(h_1=\cdots=h_c=0\) have Jacobian rank \(c\).  The Jacobian criterion in characteristic zero therefore makes their zero locus smooth of pure dimension \(d=r-c\) there.  Equivalently, after adjoining \(z\) and the equation
\[
 zH\Delta-1=0,
\]
every irreducible component of this localized system has dimension \(d\).

Choose \(d\) affine linear forms \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_d\) over \(K_G\).  There is a nonempty Zariski-open set of choices for which their common level set meets each of the finitely many base changes associated with the embeddings of \(K_G(\lambda_e)\) into \(\overline{K_G}\), and for which the resulting localized intersection is zero-dimensional.  Indeed, localization at the nonzero element \(H\Delta\) leaves each such base change nonzero; successive generic affine hyperplane sections reduce its dimension by one and remain nonempty until dimension zero.  Because \(d_e(G)<\infty\), only finitely many embeddings must be met, so the intersection of their open sets of valid choices is nonempty.

Let \(B\) be the finite quotient algebra of such a slice, with the recorded rational expression for the query adjoined when the query is not one of the \(x_i\).  Let \(\chi(t)\) be the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by that query in \(B\).  Every \(K_G\)-conjugate of \(\lambda_e\) occurs at a geometric point of the slice.  Hence the monic minimal polynomial \(p_e(t)\) divides the squarefree part of \(\chi(t)\).  Factor that squarefree part over \(K_G\).  For an irreducible factor \(q(t)\), source substitution gives
\[
 q(\lambda_e)=0\text{ in }L
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 q=p_e,
\]
because \(p_e\) is the unique monic irreducible polynomial in \(K_G[t]\) that vanishes at \(\lambda_e\).  Thus source-parametric identity testing rejects every extraneous factor and selects exactly \(p_e\).  Once this localized slice is available, multiplication-matrix linear algebra, factor testing, and the leading-coefficient, pole, infinity, and squarefreeness circuits have size \(n^{O(k+1)}\); the established degree bound gives \(\deg p_e=d_e(G)\leq2^{k+1}\), and a union bound with the established Schwartz--Zippel estimate gives symbolic error at most \(\delta\).

What is not supplied by the frozen premises is the antecedent of this reduction.  The quadratic-core lemma says that the recorded system preserves the queried projection, but it does not say that its generators span the conormal space of \(P\), that its source component is generically reduced, or that elements \(h_1,\ldots,h_c\) and a nonvanishing minor \(\Delta\) can be produced with \(n^{O(k+1)}\) circuits.  For example, a presentation may vanish to second order along its reduced source component, in which case every Jacobian minor of the displayed generators vanishes there even though the reduced prime has the expected codimension.  Computing a radical or prime component by an unrestricted elimination procedure would not establish the asserted fixed-parameter exponent.  Consequently the factor-selection step is now certified conditionally, but the source-prime-preserving localized presentation, and hence the unconditional finite output and its complete exceptional-set certificate, remain open.
